Fettle is independent. Everything we recommend comes from official UK sources, which we link to, and we turn it into a plan for your home. In an emergency, always follow official alerts.
Do I have to buy lots of stuff?
No. Many of the most important jobs are free, like joining the Priority Services Register. The rest is spread over months at a budget you choose. We never sell a doomsday kit.
I rent, or live in a flat. Is it still for me?
Yes. Flats, especially high up, have their own risks, like water pumps and lifts that need power. The plan takes that into account.
What do you do with my health answers?

They're optional, only used to build your plan, and never shared or sold. If a council or charity worker helps you make your plan, they can see it too. Only if you agree, your answers are counted in anonymous totals for your area, and small numbers are always hidden.
Yes. Fettle and The Fettle Book are available in English, Polish, Romanian, Panjabi and Urdu. Choose your language at the top of the page.
Can I make a plan for my mum?
Yes. Add another household, with their agreement, and keep both plans in one place.
Do you earn money from products you suggest?

Yes, sometimes. Some product suggestions are Amazon links, marked "paid link". As an Amazon Associate, Fettle earns from qualifying purchases, at no extra cost to you. It never changes what we recommend, and you can buy anywhere. The printed book has no shopping links.

Why this book exists, and why three days.
Most emergencies in the UK are not dramatic. A storm brings down power lines. A burst main cuts off water. Snow closes roads. Usually the lights come back within hours. Sometimes it takes days.

In {0} {1} the government launched its Be Ready campaign, asking every household to be able to look after itself for three days: water, food, warmth, light, medicines and a way to get news. Emergency services will always prioritise the most serious cases first. For everyone else, the first {2} hours are about looking after yourselves and your neighbours.
The government's own {0} survey found only {1}% of people have a household plan, and only {2}% keep three days of drinking water. If you've picked up this book, you're already ahead.
